title: He didn’t reject Jesus.
paragraphs:
He didn’t reject Jesus.
He just said… “later.”
And that was enough to lose everything.

You think delay is harmless.
You think you still have time.
But what if “later” is the most dangerous word your soul has ever whispered?

What if the greatest threat to your calling is not rebellion—
but hesitation dressed as wisdom?
Because this is where many fall… quietly.
There’s a man in Scripture who almost followed Jesus.

Not a criminal.
Not a blasphemer.
Not a mocker.
“Lord, I will follow thee; but let me first go bid them farewell…” — Luke 9:61
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable.

Because that man…
might be you.

“I’ll fully surrender after I fix my life.”
“I’ll let go of that sin when I’m stronger.”
“I’ll commit to God when things calm down.”

Sin never politely waits its turn.
And your heart?
Delayed obedience is disobedience in disguise.
Jesus didn’t comfort the man’s delay.
“No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.” — Luke 9:62
Because Jesus sees what we refuse to admit:
You cannot follow Him while negotiating your surrender.

Some scholars interpret this passage as a warning against divided loyalty—
that looking back represents a heart still tied to the old life.
What are you still holding on to?

A relationship God already told you to release?
A secret sin you’ve learned to hide well?
A version of your life where you stay in control?
But not at the cost of everything.
That’s the battlefield of your soul.
Because Jesus is not asking to be part of your life.
He is calling you to surrender it.
And here’s the truth most people avoid:
Every “later” makes your heart less responsive to God.

Conviction fades.
Sensitivity dulls.
Compromise normalizes.
But with a quiet, repeated… “not yet.”
This is not where the story ends.
The same Christ who spoke those hard words…
Walked toward a cross for people like us.

For the hesitant.
For the double-minded.
For those who delayed, denied, and ran.
“But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
While you were still in it.
And through His death and resurrection, Jesus made a way.
“For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
“For the wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23
But the verse doesn’t end there.
“…but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” — Romans 6:23
You don’t clean yourself up first.
Because Jesus didn’t say, “Follow me when you’re ready.”
So let me ask you something—no filters, no excuses:
How many times have you said “later” to God?
And what has it cost you?
That’s not guilt trying to crush you.
That’s grace trying to wake you.
And He is not asking for perfection.
Stop delaying what your soul already knows.
Pray this in your heart if you mean it:

“Lord Jesus, I’ve been saying ‘later.’
But today, I surrender.
Forgive my sin.
Change my heart.
Teach me to follow You fully.
Right now.”
